items.statement: Working capital cycle at 8 days for FY24; zero net debt with cash reserve of Rs 388 crore

items.statement: Zero net debt as of FY24 with healthy cash reserve of Rs 388 crore

items.statement: IPD segment recovery expected but not as strong; seasonal shrink business; commodity/packaging stabilization showing upward movement

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance maintained at Rs 2,500 crore with stable EBITDA margins

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of Rs 2,500 crore and stable EBITDA margins reaffirmed
items.quote: Yes, we continue, we maintain that guideline for FY '26, and also the margins, I mean, EBITDA margins are going to be stable at that number.

items.quote: There were a few customers where we were doing very small value of like trial order business where we have cracked major orders starting this season now.

items.quote: In Q4, consolidated revenues crossed INR400 crore, with EBITDA reaching INR70 crore, reflecting strong margins of 17.6%, respectively.

items.quote: Yes, certainly, these kind of disruptions are a huge headache and long-term deterrent for customers to do business with foreign geographies.

items.quote: In the time that it's not manufacturing the high value-add film, we are using it for other purposes like the regular films.

items.quote: I will not like to put any numbers again because I would not like to give a number guidance, but yes, we are operating at 90% plus capacity on our plants currently and it is impossible in a chemical plant to work at 100%.

items.quote: The inventory destocking phase, which had a significant headwind, finally came to an end leading to a notable recovery in demand, particularly from the Asia region.

items.quote: We have seen prices go down from a range of about 20% to 40% from product to product.

items.quote: That Board of Directors will take a call at suitable time.

items.statement: Wage revision from January 1, 2023 incorporated in employee costs, will stabilize by March 2024
items.quote: Last time wage revision has been done from 01/01/23. So that provision has been incorporated in the employee numbers. So till March '24 that will keep showing rise and it will stabilize.

items.statement: No visibility on government increasing fertilizer subsidy from January 2024, likely only from April
items.quote: Government is quick in reducing the subsidy but increasing it is difficult. So more or less, it will be from April onwards only.

items.statement: Expects 15-20% growth in fertilizer sales volume for FY24 vs FY23
items.quote: As I said in the morning, we are expecting 15% to 20% rise in volume in fertilizer sales this year.

items.statement: Targets FY24 revenue similar to FY23 level of INR11,368 crore
items.quote: On overall basis, we expect that we will maintain this turnover, last year turnover in this year also.

items.statement: Expects dividend income of INR140 crore in FY24 from investee companies
items.quote: No, it will be much more. It will be INR140 crores.

items.statement: Plans INR4,000 crore investment over two years for chemical business at Dahej
items.quote: So right now we are receiving a further investment of INR4,000 crores in the head for chemical business.

items.statement: Sikka unit targeting 100% capacity utilization (7.22 lakh tons) in FY24
items.quote: So in this August, we have crossed last year's June production and we hope to reach our install capacity of 7,22,000 tons, that is 100% production of install capacity and that is our target this year.

items.statement: Ammonia project commissioning by December 2023; other projects on schedule
items.quote: We will be commissioning ammonia for project by December 23, and other projects will be coming up as per the timeline mentioned.

items.statement: Sikka unit produced 2.73 lakh tons in FY23; crossed 2 lakh tons by July FY24
items.quote: This production, all the products together were 2,73,000 tons. So up to July, we have crossed 2 lakh tons.

items.statement: Q1 FY24 impacted by INR120-125 crore one-time subsidy and inventory write-downs
items.quote: So in all, around INR120 crores INR125 crores could be said to be one time effect, not really pertaining to this quarter.

items.statement: Industrial product margins improving from July; full impact visible in H2 FY24
items.quote: But as I said, full impact will be seen in H2. It is improving in this quarter. But not so much.

items.statement: Gas prices down >25% vs Q1 FY23; now stable
items.quote: It is reduced compared to, say, Q1 last year, it is more than 25% reduction. But as of now, it is stable kind of thing.

items.statement: Phosphoric acid price halved to $850/t for Jul-Sep quarter vs $1,700/t last year
items.quote: Base quarter's price is expected to be around $850, July to September. October onwards still prices are not decided. So this quarter, like last year, I mean October to December it was $1,700, now it has halved to $850, it is half now.

items.statement: Rock phosphate sourced mainly from RSMM at ~INR15,000/t; imported at INR16,000-17,000/t
items.quote: So right now, it is around INR15,000 per ton and we source one or two consignment that is totaling 60,000 tons to 70,000 tons from import sources. So that price is also, prices are quite low now in line with the phosphoric acid price. So, imported rock is also in that range only INR16,000, INR17,000.

items.statement: Sikka produces DAP, APS, NPK 10 and NPK 12; targeting 50-60% sales in Gujarat
items.quote: It is DAP, then ammonium phosphate sulphate APS, then NPK 10 and NPK 12, four products.

items.statement: No marketing issues for fertilizers; wide market reach across India with strong brand recall
items.quote: We have a good brand recall amongst the farmers, so selling is not a problem. And we, depending on the requirement, we cater to the whole country, so our market is quite wide.

items.statement: Government may calibrate subsidy from October 2023 given lower input costs
items.quote: And we also hope that looking to the economic scenario, government will calibrate the subsidy from October considering all the relevant factors and so much reduction in subsidy may or may not take place.

items.statement: Government restructuring guidelines under examination; no timeline for buyback/bonus/split decisions
items.quote: So as I said, the buyback bonus and splitting of shares, all those proposals will be examined by the GSFC Board and whatever outcome or decision is that will be announced whenever it is decided some concrete course of action.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with ~INR2,000 crore cash/FDs; INR400 crore dividend payout in September
items.quote: Yeah, so we have around INR2,000 crores cash in hand or FDs. And of course, we'll have a big obligation of dividend payment of around INR400 crores in September.

items.statement: Subsidy receivables small (INR200-300 crore); P&K paid up to July 15, urea up to June 30
items.quote: Subsidy in the books, I mean to be received from government is very small amount, may be INR200 crores, INR300 crores. In books it remains small because government considers subsidy payable only after post sale when farmer buys the fertilizer.

items.statement: Tunisia phosphoric acid JV (Stratford) operating at 30-40% capacity; expects improvement in FY25
items.quote: That plant is also not operating at optimum capacity around 30%, 40% only, they have some technical and social issues, but hopefully from next year 24-25, it should improve the performance with all whatever step they are taking for plant improvement.

items.statement: Industrial plants (caprolactam, melamine) running above 100% capacity
items.quote: All plants are working on more than 100% capacity.

items.statement: Subsidy policy erratic; retrospective reductions create unpredictability in fertilizer EBITDA
items.quote: Because whatever I produce even now, say in August, if I sell it in October, it will fetch reduced subsidy. So when we'll be able to know, farmer will take the fertilizer from retail point, it is very, very difficult to predict.

items.statement: Nano urea and nano DAP/NPK at lab scale; test marketing in FY24, commercialization later
items.quote: In case of your question for nano-urea, it's still in the lab scale at our end for manufacturing, but we are looking out for the tie-ups also. And other nano fertilizers like, DAP or NPK, it's still in the lab scale status only.

items.statement: Baroda unit fully backward integrated; Sikka unit partially integrated; both units ~10 lakh tons each
items.quote: In Baroda we are fully backward integrated. In Sikar we are in the process of getting backward integrated to some extent not fully. It will be a phase manner but yes in Baroda we are 100% backward integrated.

items.statement: Dividend consistency to be maintained in line with earnings
items.quote: Only thing I can say is that there will be consistency in dividend in line with the earnings. So if there are earnings, I think management will not hold the dividend belonging to shareholders.

items.statement: Agriculture season favorable with widespread rainfall and good reservoir levels supporting volume growth
items.quote: Season is still good because now there's a widespread rainfall as well as reservoir levels are good. And so that will occur well for rubby season also and based on that only, we see rise in the volume.

items.statement: India cheapest fertilizer market globally; imports at $100-200/t premium to domestic prices
items.quote: Price parity, if you see the prices of trade across various countries of fertilizers, India is the cheapest country, we are taking on the cheapest prices. If you go to Bangladesh also, they are still $100 more. I'm giving an average figure to you. If you go to Brazil, it is $200 more per ton on average basis.

items.statement: Shutdown maintenance cost INR25-30 crore in Q1; planned turnaround every 4 years
items.quote: So it comes to around, say, INR25 crores, INR30 crores. It depends, if you want to change major equipment and it can be more also.
